entries.finding: hint3 says 'two options fail the double-letter count... of the two left', but three options fail the cc/mm count
entries.reason: Checked against the options: A and D have one m, C has one c, so only B passes both counts. The hint's premise is false and would confuse a student counting correctly.
entries.change: hint3 rewritten: check the c's, then the m's, cross out any option failing either count, then confirm the ending has a single t. Codex's wording was not used as-is because it states outright that only one option passes.

entries.finding: exam tip says committee has 'two doubled pairs'
entries.reason: committee has three doubled letters (mm, tt, ee), so 'two doubled pairs' is wrong for it.
entries.change: Tip now says committee, embarrass and occurrence 'also have more than one doubled letter'.

entries.finding: hint3 ('which one sits right before -ity?') lets the student answer by looking at the split, without thinking
entries.reason: Once hint2 gives the rule, the draft hint3 just points at the syllable next to -ity. That fails the hint 3 test.
entries.change: hint3 replaced with Codex's fix: narrow to IM and MU and have the student compare the stress in immune with immunity said aloud.

entries.finding: hint3 'The prefix in- reverses a word's meaning' and solution 'The prefix in- means not' are unscoped absolutes
entries.reason: in- does not always mean not (income, inflammable, invaluable).
entries.change: hint3: 'The prefix in- often means not.' Solution: 'Here the prefix in- means not'.

entries.finding: tip: 'By the time plus a present verb takes will have plus the past participle' stated as a rule
entries.reason: Not always true, for example 'By the time we arrive, we will be tired.'
entries.change: Added 'usually' to both halves of the tip.

entries.finding: tip: with 'by the time' and a future event, 'choose will have plus the past participle' stated as a rule
entries.change: Tip now says will have plus the past participle 'is usually the form to choose'.

entries.reason: These groups share only an instruction line, and every item has its own sentence or word. No hint names or points to a sibling's answer.
